newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission delays review of gene-product rules.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission delays review of gene-product rules.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had postponed until the autumn a comprehensive revision of European Union rules on the release of genetically modified organisms (GMOs) into the environment.
Commission spokesman Niklaus van der Pas told a news briefing the EU's executive had not been able to make a formal decision on the complicated subject.

But it did agree guidelines on labelling all genetically modified foods for human and animal consumption. It hoped to make formal changes to EU labelling regulations on the basis of these in August, after the summer break.
"The Commission thinks it is necessary for products containing genetically modified organisms to have three sorts of labels," van der Pas said.
Producers of foodstuffs definitely or possibly containing GMOs should be obliged to label their products, using a formula of the type "This product contains GMOs" or "This product may contain GMOs".
Manufacturers could also, if they wished, explicitly label as GMO-free any products definitely not containing genetically altered substances, he said.
Van der Pas said a review of the EU's rules on labelling GMOs was necessary because some of the bloc's member states were concerned that existing rules were too lax.
